text: Over the next few lessons, the same churn finding gets built three times, in Power BI, Tableau, and Excel. That's not indecision. Each tool is going to a different audience who already trusts it.

Power BI goes to the Sales Director and leadership, since it's already the org standard with scheduled refresh built in. Tableau goes to the regional field team, who already work in it daily. Forcing them into a new tool would hurt adoption more than any feature difference would help.

Excel plays a different role. Not a deliverable, but the analyst's own independent reconciliation, built on a different engine than Power Query and DAX, so it's a genuine second opinion. And all three tools read the exact same T-SQL active and churned definition. One definition, three presentations, never three guesses.
Writing this down up front sets real boundaries. Excel never gets published, Tableau doesn't replace the executive view, and Power BI doesn't become the field team's daily driver.
Three audiences, three tools, one source of truth. Next: planning the SQL query itself, before Power BI even opens.
